transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what brought me in is that I find myself checking the same things over and over before I can move on. It's mostly boxes, my lists, and the drawers around our condo. 

I'll check them repeatedly, even though I know perfectly well I already looked. It's getting a bit frustrating because my wife will be waiting for me to just leave it be and get going, but I get stuck doing it. So, I figured it was time to come in and see what can be done about it.
When you're checking these boxes, lists, and drawers repeatedly, do you recognize that the checking doesn't really make sense, or does it feel necessary and justified to you?

I know it doesn't make sense. I mean, like I mentioned, I know perfectly well I already looked at that list or checked that drawer. Logically, I know it's silly. 

But... it just feels like I can't move on until I do it again. So, no, it doesn't feel justified or necessary in a practical way. It's just something I get stuck doing, even when my wife is standing right there waiting for me to just leave it be so we can leave the condo. I know better, but I just keep doing it anyway.

Before you feel the urge to check these boxes, lists, and drawers, do you experience any intrusive thoughts or worries — like a fear that something bad might happen, or a feeling that things aren't quite right — that makes you feel like you have to check?

Yes, that's exactly it. I keep getting these... well, these nagging thoughts. It's usually a worry that I might have accidentally thrown away something important from my old teaching files, or maybe that I put a needed tool in the wrong box. 

I'll tell myself it's highly unlikely, but the thought just keeps coming back anyway. It just makes it really hard to settle down and relax until I go and look.

Besides these checking urges, do you experience other intrusive thoughts or worries that feel unwanted — for example, thoughts about contamination, harm, or things needing to be in a particular order — that don't necessarily lead to checking?

No, not really. It's just the checking that I mentioned. I don't worry about germs or getting sick, and I don't have any fears about hurting anyone or anything like that. And I don't care if things are lined up perfectly or in a certain order. It's really just the nagging feeling that I misplaced something important, which leads to the checking. So, no other thoughts like the ones you're describing.
How long have you been experiencing these checking urges and the nagging thoughts about misplacing things? Has this been going on for several weeks, months, or longer?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of exactly when it started. 

I mean, it's been going on for a while, but... I couldn't tell you if it's been a few weeks, or a few months, or what. It just sort of crept up on me, I guess. So, yeah, I don't really have a specific timeline for you.
When you think back to when this checking started, would you say it's been happening for at least a couple of weeks or longer?

Well, yes, I suppose it's been at least a couple of weeks. Probably longer. Like I said, I just... I really haven't kept track of it. It didn't happen all at once, so I can't give you an exact date, but it's definitely been going on for more than just a few days.

You mentioned your wife gets frustrated waiting for you. Beyond that, how much would you say these checking urges and the nagging thoughts are interfering with your daily life, work, or relationships? Are they causing you significant distress?

Well, it is getting in the way of a few things. Unpacking the condo, for example, has taken much longer than it really should. And... I've been putting off my preparation for my tutoring at the library, and even just my regular hobbies. I just get this feeling that I can't move on to doing those other things until everything is verified enough. So, yes, it is frustrating to deal with.

When you try to resist the urge to check those boxes, lists, or drawers — say, when your wife asks you to just leave and come with her — do you feel a buildup of anxiety or tension that only goes away once you've checked?

Well, yes, that's exactly it. If I try to just walk away, that tense feeling really builds up. 

Honestly, that's a big part of what brought me in to see you. I find myself checking the same boxes, my lists, the condo drawers over and over again before I can finally move on. And the frustrating thing is, I know perfectly well I already looked. But even when my wife is standing right there, waiting for me to just leave it be and come with her, I still have to go back and do it. The tension doesn't really go away until I check one last time.

F42.1 (OCD with predominantly obsessional thoughts) and F42.9 (OCD unspecified) included as broader OCD categories. F41.1 (Generalized anxiety disorder) included as anxiety can present with repetitive behaviors. F60.5 (Obsessive-compulsive personality disorder) included but less likely given acute presentation and ego-dystonic nature of symptoms.
